definitions.explanation: Leaving one's current place of residence to move to a different area, especially in the context of official registration.
Being transferred from one workplace, school, or organization to another.

examples.japanese: {転出届|てんしゅつとどけ}を{出|だ}す。
{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{際|さい}には{転出|てんしゅつ}{手続|てつづ}きが{必要|ひつよう}です。
examples.english: A moving-out procedure is required when relocating.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{若者|わかもの}の{転出|てんしゅつ}が{止|と}まらず、{人口|じんこう}が{減|へ}り{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: In this area, the outflow of young people hasn't stopped, and the population keeps declining.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{大阪支社|おおさかししゃ}に{転出|てんしゅつ}した。
examples.english: He was transferred to the Osaka branch.

examples.japanese: {転出先|てんしゅつさき}の{学校|がっこう}で{友達|ともだち}ができた。
examples.english: I made friends at the school I transferred to.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}な{転出|てんしゅつ}が{決|き}まり、{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎに{追|お}われた。
examples.english: A sudden transfer was decided, and I was scrambling to hand over my duties.

notes:
{転|てん} (move, change) + {出|しゅつ} (exit, leave). The word emphasizes leaving or departing from a current location, as opposed to arriving at a new one.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {転出届|てんしゅつとどけ} — moving-out notification (submitted to city hall)
- {転出先|てんしゅつさき} — destination of the move or transfer
- {転出|てんしゅつ}{手続|てつづ}き — moving-out procedures
- {転出|てんしゅつ}{証明書|しょうめいしょ} — moving-out certificate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {転入|てんにゅう} — moving in; transfer into — the opposite: arriving at a new location
- {転居|てんきょ} — change of residence — more general, focuses on the move itself rather than departure
- {転勤|てんきん} — job transfer — specifically a workplace reassignment to a different office
